scenes.headline: How a tiny model holds a long window
scenes.sub: and what reward alone taught it
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pipkin. I read quark's config, its weights and its report.

states.say: Sixteen layers, seven hundred and sixty-eight wide.

states.term: Local layer: attention over the last 256 tokens
states.say: Three local layers, then one global, four times over. Only the global layers look at the whole context.

steps.label: local: a 256-token window
steps.say: A local layer sees a short window, with a small convolution beside it. Its memory never grows.

steps.label: global: every earlier token
steps.say: A global layer sees everything before it. Twelve query heads share four key and value heads.
Attention and the convolution run side by side, and a learned weight blends them.

steps.caption: only these four caches grow with context
steps.say: The global layer is plain grouped-query attention. Its cache is the one that grows.
Pretraining ran five hundred billion tokens on one eight-GPU node, the context growing stage by stage.
The thirty-two thousand token stage was mostly synthetic retrieval and tracking tasks.

steps.term: RoPE base: how slowly positions rotate
steps.say: Then a branch trained at a hundred and twenty-eight thousand. The global layers' rotary base went from five hundred thousand to four million.

scenes.title: Cache for one 128K sequence, GB
scenes.say: About half a gigabyte of cache at full length. Make every layer global and it is about ten times more.

scenes.title: Reward needs one success per group

steps.label: Early: 2.6% solved
steps.say: Reinforcement learning used GRPO. Each prompt gets a group of replies, checked by code. If they all fail, the group teaches nothing.

steps.label: One success in a group
steps.term: Advantage: reward minus the group's mean
steps.say: One success is enough. The passing reply is pushed up and the failures are pushed down.

steps.label: Never valid: 0%
steps.say: One harness never produced a valid call. With no success to compare against, it never learned.

steps.label: Late harness: 42% in its first steps
steps.say: Harnesses added late started near half solved in their first hundred steps, so almost every group carried a signal.

steps.caption: 2.6% to 64.5% across 15 harnesses
steps.say: Across fifteen emulated coding harnesses, simple terminal tasks went from under three percent solved to about two thirds.
These are training rollouts, not a held-out test.

scenes.title: Arithmetic, pass@1 in %
scenes.note: base: 39 of 40 prompts right at least once
scenes.say: I ran both models on arithmetic. The base already got thirty-nine of forty prompts right somewhere in sixteen tries. RL made it right more often. It sharpened a skill that was there.

items.say: The base model already wrote tool calls. Offered a calculator, it called it nineteen times in twenty, with a placeholder for the argument.
The RL objective kept a small supervised term, on steps written by code.
And no fine-tuned model of the same size was run on the same tasks.

scenes.text: Pretraining planted the tool format. Reward turned it into a skill, on simple tasks.
scenes.mark: Reward turned it into a skill
scenes.say: Pretraining planted the tool format. Reward turned a handful of right answers into a skill, on simple tasks.

recap: 4 of 16 layers see the whole context
